C.Ebrahim Haji vs Vatakara Muncipality on 6 February, 2024 
Author: P.V.Kunhikrishnan
Bench: P.V.Kunhikrishnan
 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
 Present
 The Honourable Mr. Justice P.V.Kunhikrishnan
 Tuesday, The 6Th Day Of February 2024 / 17Th Magha, 1945

Petitioner:
 C.Ebrahim Haji
 Aged 59 Years

 Mukkolabhagam, Vatakara, Kozhikode Dist
 By Advs.
 Sri.K.P.Sudheer
 Sri.Arun Mathew Vadakkan
Respondents:
 1 Vatakara Muncipality
 Vatakara, Pin-673101,Rep By Its Secretary
 2 Municipal Council
 Vatakara Municipality, Vatakara-673101, Rep By
 Its Chairman
 By Adv Sri.T.Naveen, Sc, Vatakara Municipality

Admission On 06.02.2024, The Court On The Same Day

 P.V.Kunhikrishnan, J.

 Dated this the 6th day of February, 2024.
 Judgment
This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking the following reliefs:
C.Ebrahim Haji vs Vatakara Muncipality on 6 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95766706/ 
1 (a) Call for the records leading to Exts.P5, p7 and P9 orders and quash the same by issuing a writ of certiorari or any other writ, order or direction. 
(b) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction commanding the respondents not to cancel the licence issued to the petitioner in respect of retail meat shop functioning in Stall No.4 of Ward No.30 of 1st respondent Municipality. 
(c) Issue such other writ, order or direction as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case. 
2. Petitioner is a resident of 1 st respondent Municipality. It is the case of the petitioner that for the last twenty five years, he is conducting business of sale of meat in Stall No.4 of Ward No.30 of the 1 st respondent Municipality. The business is being conducted after obtaining requisite licence from the Municipality. It is submitted that the petitioner and his family are depending on the income derived from the said business. According to the petitioner, at the instance of business rivals,
proceedings were initiated against the petitioner's business in animal hide and Ext.P1 is the final order passed by the Tribunal in such proceedings. It is the definite case of the petitioner that false complaint was registered against the petitioner and Ext.P2 show cause notice dated 24.8.2013 was issued by the 1 st respondent. and the petitioner submitted Ext.P4 objection on 26.8.2013. As directed by the Municipality, the petitioner also submitted a representation dated 24.8.2013, is the submission. Thereafter, without affording an opportunity of hearing and without adverting to Ext.P4 objection submitted by the petitioner, Ext.P5 order dated 30.8.2013 was passed, is the submission. By Ext.P5 order, the licence issued to the petitioner's business was temporarily cancelled. 
3. The petitioner filed a statutory appeal and a petition for stay of the proceedings. Since no orders are passed on the stay petition, the petitioner filed W.P. No.22908 of 2015 before this Court. By Ext.P6 judgment, this Court directed the Municipality to consider and pass orders in the stay petition. Even before getting a certified copy of the judgment, the petitioner was served with a notice dated 10.9.2013 to appear for a hearing in the appeal, is the submission. Even though, the petitioner sought two weeks time for hearing, the said request was rejected and the hearing was completed on 19.9.2013. By Ext.P7 communication, the petitioner was informed that the appeal filed by him was rejected by the 2nd respondent on 25.9.2013. Even though, the petitioner was not served with the decision dated 25.9.2013, it is submitted that, the petitioner filed a Revision Petition No.170 of 2013 before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions, Thiruvananthapuram. 
4. Ext.P8 is the interim order passed by the Tribunal staying the implementation of Ext.P5 order. 
Now by Ext.P9 order, the Tribunal rejected the revision petition. Ext.P10 is the report submitted by the Food Safety Officer during the pendency of the revision petition, is the submission. According to the petitioner, it would show that the petitioner is selling only wholesome and stamped meat obtained from the authorised slaughter house. Hence, this writ petition is filed. 
5. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the Municipality. 
C.Ebrahim Haji vs Vatakara Muncipality on 6 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95766706/
2 6. A counter affidavit is filed by the Municipality. When this writ petition came up for consideration on 12.9.2014, an interim order was passed by this Court staying Ext.P5 order and the operation of Ext.P9 order. Based on the above interim order, the petitioner is continuing his business, is the submission of the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 1 st respondent Municipality. 
Moreover, there is no case for the 1 st respondent that the petitioner has committed any similar activity as stated in Ext.P5 order subsequent to the interim order passed by this Court. But it is also submitted that, based on the interim order, the petitioner is continuing the business without paying the licence fee and the petitioner has to pay the arrears of licence fee immediately because the shop belongs to the Municipality. 
7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this writ petition can be disposed of setting aside the impugned orders and directing the petitioner to pay the arrears of licence fee as on today,
within two months from today. Petitioner is free to approach the Municipality for renewal of licence and if any such application is submitted, the Municipality will consider the same in accordance with law. Therefore, the writ petition is disposed of with the following directions:
(1) Exts.P5 and P9 orders are set aside. 
(2) Petitioner is directed to pay the arrears of licence fee as on today within two months from today. 
(3) Petitioner is free to submit an application for renewal of licence before the 1st respondent Municipality and if any such application is submitted, the 1st respondent will consider the same in accordance with law and on condition that the petitioner will pay the arrears of licence as on today, within two months as ordered above. 
Sd/-
